edges.effect_quant: The evidence remains contested: large nonrandomized screening-program analyses do not show a clear population melanoma mortality benefit, but case-control and thickness-based studies suggest that clinician whole-body skin examination may reduce the incidence of thicker melanomas that drive death risk.
edges.population: asymptomatic adolescents and adults undergoing routine clinician or dermatologist whole-body skin examination for melanoma screening
edges.mechanism: Visual whole-body skin examination may detect melanoma at thinner, earlier stages when excision is more curative, but the pathway is vulnerable to lead-time bias, overdiagnosis, and inconsistent implementation across clinicians and health systems.
edges.summary: This edge is genuinely split rather than simply weak. The modern USPSTF-linked evidence review found little to no clear population mortality benefit, yet supportive observational work still suggests a plausible stage-shift advantage, so a mixed label is more honest than forcing either a reassuring or dismissive conclusion.
edges.caveats: There are no randomized trials, so the entire literature is exposed to selection bias, lead-time bias, and ecological confounding. This edge addresses melanoma mortality rather than the separate questions of thin-lesion detection, overdiagnosis, biopsy burden, or cosmetic harms.

evidence.notes: Skin Cancer Screening: Updated Evidence Report and Systematic Review for the US Preventive Services Task Force.

effect_quant.comparator: participants in the 2 German population-based screening programs providing direct mortality evidence; overall review included 6,053,411 people

evidence.citation: Aitken JF et al 2010 Int J Cancer
evidence.notes: Clinical whole-body skin examination reduces the incidence of thick melanomas.

effect_quant.comparator: whole-body clinical skin examination in the prior 3 years versus no examination for diagnosis of thick melanoma

evidence.citation: Boniol M et al 2015 BMJ Open
evidence.notes: Melanoma mortality following skin cancer screening in Germany.
